Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 3a) demonstrates a right-sided pneumothorax with the visceral pleura separated from the chest wall, causing the azygos lobe to shift laterally away from the mediastinum. In this displaced position, the characteristic teardrop-shaped opacity of the azygos vein is no longer visible at the caudal end of the fissure, leaving the fissure appearing empty or distinct against the air-filled pleural space.
